questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture had to be different from the danish culture. It had to be a unique place that I had not been to before. It had to be a country where the population was good at speaking English. It had to have good living conditions.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a great opportunity to do something different. I would recommend it to everybody.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy. It helped a lot to talk to people who had done it before myself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University I went to was supportive and helpful. They held events and gave a lot of information about the country and city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Plenty of opportunities to get all the information needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There are many places to live and most places seem to be good. However, the housing market is expensive so be prepared to pay a lot. I would recommend to talk to someone who did it before yourself and hear if they have anything to potentially overtake or if they can recommend something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really expensive. Public transport is good in Sydney but it always takes 30 minutes or more no matter where you stay if you have to take public transport to the university. There are many great areas that offer different things. I do recommend staying off campus if you have someone to live with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I was very satisfied but I also found something quickly and not the most expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to registrer for me. It is easy to email the university and they answer quickly. However, other people who took more popular courses had more issues.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a big coursebook with all the old courses they have offered. I found the courses that I liked and looked if they were offered again and if they were offered in the right semester. I then signed up for them. Some courses will be filled up quickly. They give you some courses that you can choose from. I did not like any of them but for me it was easy to get access to the courses that I wanted after filling a waiver. You have to do a lot of research yourself if you want some good courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university had someone you could call or email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was able to register for all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do a lot of research and do it early so you can get the right courses. Also, you can always change course before one to two weeks into the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The math level is not the highest but it seems like they have something for most people.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was not the hardest. This is due to the fact that you constantly get evaluated throughout the semester with quizzes and assignments. If you do well in these things you have set yourself up for a good grade even before the final exam if there even is that in your course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many more quizzes and assignments during the semester. They were really helpful and tried to explain everything  in an easy way. They were more pedagogical than at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced Bayesian Methods
Advanced Machine Learning Application
Machine Learning: Mathematical Theory and Application

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It would recommend all the courses that I took. Advanced Bayesian Methods had a great teacher and you will learn a lot, some people might prefer if it was more in depth. Advanced Machine Learning Application is great for coding and actually building something useful. However, it had no math. Machine Learning: Mathematical Theory and Application had the most math, but it was not that much. The teacher is great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Cost for some school events.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was more expensive than I though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are so many opportunities so do something fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The school offered a ton of events. Events to see the city, go travel, surfing, cultural events, parties, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend all of them. I would go to as many as possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to blue mountains, surfing, figure eight pools, roadtrip on the east coast, to the outback, to Tasmania, Melbourne, all the beaches, go hiking, go climbing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is easy. Similar to Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be hard to find local students. They mostly put all the exchange students together. Maybe join a club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everyone in Sydney wakes up really early because the sun rises early in the morning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the life style. Everyone is laid back and easy going.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join as many clubs as possible. Try to be outgoing in the beginning especially. Have an open and positive mind.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Australia (especially nature) and meeting new people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Planning everything and getting the most out of the time I had.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
